title: We revile neither statues nor demons
source_text: Εἶτα ὡς αἱ γρᾶες διαλοιδορούμενος ἡμῖν φησι· σὺ μὲν τὰ ἀγάλματα τούτων λοιδορῶν καταγελᾷς. ὡς αὐτόν γε τὸν Διόνυσον ἢ τὸν Ἡρακλέα παρόντα εἰ ἐλοιδόρησας, οὐκ ἂν ἴσως χαίρων ἀπήλλαξας· τὸν δὲ σὸν θεὸν παρόντα κατατείνοντες καὶ κολάζοντες οὐδὲν οἱ ταῦτα δράσαντες πεπόνθασιν ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐν τοσούτῳ βίῳ. τί καινὸν ἐξ ἐκείνου γέγονε τῷ πιστεύσαντι ἂν ὡς οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖνος ἄνθρωπος γόης ἀλλὰ θεοῦ παῖς; καὶ ὁ πέμψας ἄρα τὸν υἱὸν ἀγγελμάτων τινῶν εἵνεκα οὕτως ὠμῶς κολασθέντα, ὡς συνδιαφθεῖραι καὶ τὰ ἀγγέλματα, περιεῖδε καὶ τοσούτου χρόνου διελθόντος οὐκ ἐπεστράφη. τίς οὕτως ἀνόσιος πατήρ; ἐκεῖνος μὲν οὖν τυχὸν ἐβούλετο, ὡς φῂς, διὰ τοῦτο περιϋβρίζετο. οἵδε δὲ, οὓς σὺ βλασφημεῖς, ἐνῆν μὲν εἰπεῖν ὅτι καὶ αὐτοὶ βούλονται καὶ διὰ τοῦτ᾿ ἀνέχονται βλασφημούμενοι· τὰ γὰρ ἴσα τοῖς ἴσοις παραβαλεῖν κράτιστον· ἀλλ᾿ οὗτοί γε καὶ σφόδρα ἀμύνονται τὸν βλασφημοῦντα, ἤτοι φεύγοντα διὰ τοῦτο καὶ κρυπτόμενον ἢ ἁλισκόμενον καὶ ἀπολλύμενον. καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα δ᾿ εἴποιμ᾿ ἂν ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐδενὶ λοιδορούμεθα, πειθόμενοι ὅτι „λοίδοροι“ „βασιλείαν θεοῦ“ οὐ „κληρονομήσουσι,“ καὶ ἀναγινώσκοντες τὸ „εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμῖν“ (καὶ) „εὐλογεῖτε καὶ μὴ καταρᾶσθε.“ εἰδότες δὲ καὶ τὸ „λοιδορούμενοι εὐλογοῦμεν.“ καὶ εἴπερ τὸ λοιδορεῖν λόγον τινὰ ἔχει ἀμυντικὸν τοῦ δοκοῦντος ἠδικῆσθαι, καὶ οὐδὲ τοῦτον ἐπιτρέπει ἡμῖν ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος· πόσῳ πλέον, ἔνθα πολλὴν ἠλιθιότητα ἐμφαίνει τὸ λοιδορεῖν, οὐ χρὴ λοιδορεῖν; ἐπ᾿ ἴσης δὲ ἠλίθιον τὸ λοιδορεῖσθαι λίθῳ ἢ χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ, τοῖς μεμορφωμένοις εἰς τὴν νενομισμένην τοῖς μακρὰν θειότητος τυγχάνουσι θεῶν μορφήν. οὕτω δὲ οὐδὲ καταγελῶμεν τῶν ἀψύχων ξοάνων ἀλλ᾿ εἰ ἄρα τῶν προσκυνούντων αὐτοῖς. ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿, ἂν ὦσί τινες δαίμονες ἐνιδρυμένοι τισὶν ἀγάλμασι, καὶ νομίζηται ὁ μέν τις αὐτῶν εἶναι Διόνυσος ὁ δ᾿ Ἡρακλῆς, οὐδὲ τούτοις λοιδορούμεθα· μάταιον γὰρ τὸ τοιοῦτον καὶ οὐδαμῶς κατὰ τὸν πρᾷον καὶ εἰρηναῖον καὶ γαληνὸν τὴν ψυχὴν καὶ μαθόντα ὅτι οὐδὲ διὰ τὴν κακίαν δεῖ τινι λοιδορεῖσθαι, εἴτ᾿ ἀνθρώπῳ εἴτε δαίμονι.
pass_a_gloss: Then, like old women (γρᾶες) railing at us (διαλοιδορούμενος), he says: you, reviling (λοιδορῶν) the statues (ἀγάλματα) of these, laugh (καταγελᾷς). Whereas if you had reviled Dionysus himself or Heracles being present (παρόντα), perhaps you would not have gone off rejoicing (χαίρων ἀπήλλαξας = got off unpunished); but those who stretched out (κατατείνοντες) and punished (κολάζοντες) your God being present suffered nothing (οὐδὲν πεπόνθασιν), nor even afterwards in so long a life (ἐν τοσούτῳ βίῳ). What new thing (καινόν) has happened since then for one who would believe that he was not a man sorcerer (ἄνθρωπος γόης) but a child of God (θεοῦ παῖς)? And the one who sent his son for the sake of certain messages (ἀγγελμάτων), punished so cruelly (ὠμῶς) as to destroy the messages along with him (συνδιαφθεῖραι), overlooked it (περιεῖδε) and, so much time having passed, did not turn (οὐκ ἐπεστράφη). What father is so unholy (ἀνόσιος)? Now he perhaps wished it (ἐβούλετο), as you say; for this reason he was outraged (περιϋβρίζετο). But these whom you blaspheme (βλασφημεῖς): it was possible to say that they too wish it and for this reason endure (ἀνέχονται) being blasphemed; for to compare equals with equals (τὰ ἴσα τοῖς ἴσοις παραβαλεῖν) is best; but these at any rate vigorously avenge themselves on (σφόδρα ἀμύνονται) the blasphemer, who either flees for this reason and hides, or is caught (ἁλισκόμενον) and perishes. And to this I would say that we revile no one, persuaded that revilers (λοίδοροι) will not inherit (κληρονομήσουσι) the kingdom of God, and reading 'bless those who curse (καταρωμένους) you' and 'bless and do not curse', and knowing also 'being reviled we bless'. And if reviling has some ground (λόγον) of self-defence (ἀμυντικόν) for one who seems to have been wronged, and the word of God (ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος) does not permit (ἐπιτρέπει) us even this, how much more, where reviling displays (ἐμφαίνει) much folly (ἠλιθιότητα), must one not revile? Equally foolish is to revile stone or gold or silver, things shaped (μεμορφωμένοις) into the form of gods customary (νενομισμένην) to those who are far from divinity (θειότητος). So we do not laugh at the lifeless wooden images (ἀψύχων ξοάνων), but, if at all, at those who worship (προσκυνούντων) them. But not even if there are some demons (δαίμονες) seated in (ἐνιδρυμένοι) certain statues, and one of them is thought (νομίζηται) to be Dionysus and another Heracles, do we revile these; for such a thing is futile (μάταιον) and in no way befits the one gentle (πρᾷον), peaceable (εἰρηναῖον) and calm (γαληνόν) in soul, and who has learned that one must not revile anyone even on account of wickedness (κακίαν), whether man or demon.
pass_b_english: Next, railing at us like old women, he says: “You revile their statues and laugh at them. But if you had reviled Dionysus himself or Heracles while he was present, perhaps you would not have got away with it. Yet those who stretched out and punished your God when he was present suffered nothing for doing it, nor even afterwards, in all the long life that followed. What new thing has happened since then to make anyone believe that he was not a human sorcerer but a child of God? And the one who sent his son for the sake of certain messages, it seems, looked on while he was punished so cruelly that the messages were destroyed with him, and in all the time that has passed since then he has paid no heed. What father is so unholy? Now perhaps he wished it, as you say, and that is why he suffered outrage. But as for these whom you blaspheme, one could have said that they too wish it, and for that reason bear being blasphemed; for it is best to compare like with like. But these at least take vigorous vengeance on the one who blasphemes them, so that he either flees for this reason and hides, or is caught and perishes.”

To this I would answer that we revile no one, for we are persuaded that “revilers” will not “inherit the kingdom of God” (1 Corinthians 6:10), and we read, “Bless those who curse you” (Luke 6:28), and, “Bless, and do not curse” (Romans 12:14). We know also the saying, “When reviled, we bless” (1 Corinthians 4:12). And if reviling has some justification as self-defence for one who thinks he has been wronged, yet the word of God does not allow us even this, how much more must we refrain from reviling where reviling shows great folly? It is equally foolish to revile stone or gold or silver, shaped into the form of gods that is customary among those who are far from the divine. So we do not laugh at the lifeless images either, but, if at anyone, at those who worship them.

Nor, even if there are demons settled in certain statues, and one of them is thought to be Dionysus and another Heracles, do we revile them either. Such a thing is futile, and in no way fits the man who is gentle, peaceable and calm of soul, and who has learned that one must not revile anyone, man or demon, even for his wickedness.

choices.choice: ‘Their statues’ (τὰ ἀγάλματα τούτων): τούτων points back to the gods named in Celsus’s preceding text; left as ‘their’. Celsus’s ‘your God’ and ‘child of God’ (θεοῦ παῖς) refer to the Christian God and are capitalised; ‘his son’ in Celsus’s mouth is left lower case, since he speaks of the Christian claim with scorn. ‘Stretched out’ (κατατείνοντες) means stretching for torture or on the cross. ἐκεῖνος ... ἐβούλετο: ‘he’ is taken as Jesus, who (Celsus reports the Christian claim) willed his sufferings. ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος here means God’s teaching in Scripture, so ‘word’ is kept lower case. Luke 6:28 also matches the Western text of Matthew 5:44; Luke cited. ‘Must not revile anyone ... even for his wickedness, whether man or demon’ is a likely allusion to Jude 9 (Michael did not bring a reviling judgement against the devil); not cited inline because no words are quoted. The Greek repeats the Celsus quotation in 43; the two renderings are kept identical. παρόντα is rendered ‘while he was present’ / ‘when he was present’ (not ‘to his face’ or ‘in person’), because Origen’s reply in 42 turns on that word (‘how one who is not present hears anything’).
παρόντα: 'to his face' / 'in person' changed to 'while he was present' / 'when he was present', so Origen's reply in 42 about presence connects
ἀγγελμάτων τινῶν εἵνεκα: 'with certain messages' changed to 'for the sake of certain messages' (matches 43)
συνδιαφθεῖραι: 'the messages perished with him' changed to 'were destroyed with him', to match Origen's διέφθειρε 'did not destroy' in 43
λόγον τινὰ ἀμυντικόν: 'some show of reason' changed to 'some justification'
Scripture checked: 1 Corinthians 6:10, Luke 6:28, Romans 12:14, 1 Corinthians 4:12 all match
